title: Higher-Order, Laplace & Systems
description: Second-order linear equations, characteristic roots, undetermined coefficients, variation of parameters, oscillators and resonance, Laplace transforms, linear systems and phase portraits, and series solutions.

cards.title: Standard form of a second-order **linear** ODE?
cards.body:
$y'' + p(t)\,y' + q(t)\,y = g(t)$

It is **homogeneous** when $g \equiv 0$ and **nonhomogeneous** otherwise.

Example: $y'' + 4y = \cos t$ is linear, constant-coefficient and nonhomogeneous; $y'' + y^2 = 0$ is nonlinear.
cards.searchQuery: second order linear ODE standard form homogeneous

cards.title: **Superposition principle** for $y'' + py' + qy = 0$?
cards.body:
If $y_1$ and $y_2$ are solutions, then so is $c_1y_1 + c_2y_2$ for any constants.

Watch out: it fails for nonhomogeneous equations and for nonlinear ones. The sum of two solutions of $y'' + y = 1$ is not a solution.
cards.searchQuery: superposition principle linear homogeneous ODE

cards.title: **Wronskian** of two functions $y_1, y_2$?
cards.body:
$W(y_1, y_2) = y_1 y_2' - y_1' y_2 = \begin{vmatrix} y_1 & y_2 \\ y_1' & y_2' \end{vmatrix}$

For two solutions of a second-order homogeneous ODE, $W \ne 0$ means they are linearly independent.

Mnemonic: first times derivative of second, minus derivative of first times second.
cards.searchQuery: Wronskian definition two functions determinant

cards.title: Wronskian of $y_1 = e^{t}$ and $y_2 = e^{2t}$? (type in $t$)
cards.body:
$e^{3t}$

$W = e^{t}\cdot 2e^{2t} - e^{t}\cdot e^{2t} = 2e^{3t} - e^{3t} = e^{3t}$.

It is never zero, so the two functions are independent.
cards.searchQuery: Wronskian of e^t and e^2t

cards.title: What is a **fundamental set of solutions** of a second-order linear homogeneous ODE?
cards.body:
Two solutions $y_1, y_2$ with $W(y_1,y_2) \ne 0$.

Then every solution is $y = c_1y_1 + c_2y_2$.

Key idea: the solution space is a 2-dimensional vector space and $\{y_1,y_2\}$ is a basis.
cards.searchQuery: fundamental set of solutions linear homogeneous ODE

cards.title: What is the dimension of the solution space of an order-$n$ linear homogeneous ODE? (in terms of $n$)
cards.body:
$n$

It takes $n$ independent solutions, matching the $n$ initial conditions $y(t_0), \dots, y^{(n-1)}(t_0)$.

Example: a second-order equation has a 2-dimensional solution space.
cards.searchQuery: dimension of solution space linear homogeneous ODE order n

cards.title: **Abel's theorem** for the Wronskian of solutions of $y'' + p(t)y' + q(t)y = 0$?
cards.body:
$W(t) = C\,e^{-\int p(t)\,dt}$

So $W$ is either identically zero or never zero on an interval where $p$ is continuous.

Why: differentiating gives $W' = -pW$, a first-order linear ODE.
cards.searchQuery: Abel's theorem Wronskian formula second order ODE

cards.title: If two solutions of a second-order linear homogeneous ODE have $W(t_0) = 0$ at one point, what follows?
cards.body:
They are linearly dependent, and $W \equiv 0$ everywhere.

By Abel's theorem $W$ cannot vanish at just one point.

Watch out: this applies to solutions of the same ODE; arbitrary functions can have $W(t_0)=0$ at one point and still be independent.
cards.searchQuery: Wronskian zero at one point solutions linearly dependent

cards.title: For $ay'' + by' + cy = 0$ (constants), what is the **characteristic equation**?
cards.body:
$ar^2 + br + c = 0$

Substitute $y = e^{rt}$: $y' = re^{rt}$ and $y'' = r^2e^{rt}$, then divide by $e^{rt} \ne 0$.

Key idea: calculus becomes algebra; the roots $r$ give the solutions.
cards.searchQuery: characteristic equation constant coefficient second order ODE

cards.title: General solution of $ay'' + by' + cy = 0$ when the roots $r_1 \ne r_2$ are real?
cards.body:
$y = c_1e^{r_1t} + c_2e^{r_2t}$

Here $b^2 - 4ac > 0$, and the two exponentials are independent ($W \ne 0$).

Example: roots $1$ and $-1$ give $y = c_1e^{t} + c_2e^{-t}$.
cards.searchQuery: distinct real roots characteristic equation general solution

cards.title: Characteristic roots of $y'' - 5y' + 6y = 0$? (list)
cards.searchQuery: characteristic roots y'' - 5y' + 6y = 0

cards.title: General solution of $ay'' + by' + cy = 0$ with a repeated root $r$?
cards.body:
$y = (c_1 + c_2 t)\,e^{rt}$

Here $b^2 - 4ac = 0$ and $r = -\dfrac{b}{2a}$.

Watch out: writing $c_1e^{rt} + c_2e^{rt}$ gives only one independent solution; the second needs the factor $t$.
cards.searchQuery: repeated root characteristic equation te^(rt) general solution

cards.title: Why is $te^{rt}$ a solution when $r$ is a double root?
cards.body:
A double root means $p(r) = 0$ and $p'(r) = 0$ for the characteristic polynomial $p$.

For $y = te^{rt}$, $L[y] = p(r)\,te^{rt} + p'(r)\,e^{rt} = 0$.

Check with $y'' - 2y' + y = 0$: $y = te^{t}$ gives $(t+2)e^t - 2(t+1)e^t + te^t = 0$.
cards.searchQuery: why t e^(rt) second solution repeated root reduction of order

cards.title: General solution of $y'' + 6y' + 9y = 0$? (type with $c_1, c_2$)
cards.body:
$y = (c_1 + c_2t)e^{-3t}$

$r^2 + 6r + 9 = (r+3)^2$, so $r = -3$ is a double root.
cards.searchQuery: solve y'' + 6y' + 9y = 0 double root

cards.title: General real solution when the characteristic roots are $\alpha \pm i\beta$?
cards.body:
$y = e^{\alpha t}\left(c_1\cos\beta t + c_2\sin\beta t\right)$

Here $b^2 - 4ac < 0$, with $\alpha = -\dfrac{b}{2a}$ and $\beta = \dfrac{\sqrt{4ac - b^2}}{2a}$.

Key idea: $\alpha$ sets growth or decay; $\beta$ sets the oscillation frequency.
cards.searchQuery: complex roots characteristic equation e^(alpha t) cos sin solution

cards.title: How does Euler's formula turn $e^{(\alpha + i\beta)t}$ into real solutions?
cards.body:
$e^{(\alpha+i\beta)t} = e^{\alpha t}(\cos\beta t + i\sin\beta t)$.

The real part $e^{\alpha t}\cos\beta t$ and the imaginary part $e^{\alpha t}\sin\beta t$ are each real solutions.

Why: the equation has real coefficients, so real and imaginary parts of a complex solution each solve it.
cards.searchQuery: Euler formula complex exponential real solutions ODE

cards.title: General solution of $y'' + 4y = 0$? (type with $c_1, c_2$)
cards.body:
$y = c_1\cos 2t + c_2\sin 2t$

The roots of $r^2 + 4 = 0$ are $r = \pm 2i$, so $\alpha = 0$ and $\beta = 2$.
cards.searchQuery: solve y'' + 4y = 0 general solution cos 2t sin 2t

cards.title: Characteristic roots of $y'' + 2y' + 5y = 0$? (list)
cards.body:
$r = -1 \pm 2i$

Quadratic formula: $r = \dfrac{-2 \pm \sqrt{4 - 20}}{2} = -1 \pm 2i$.

So $y = e^{-t}(c_1\cos 2t + c_2\sin 2t)$, a decaying oscillation.
cards.searchQuery: characteristic roots y'' + 2y' + 5y = 0 complex

cards.title: Match the sign of $b^2 - 4ac$ to the form of solutions of $ay'' + by' + cy = 0$.
cards.body:
- $> 0$: two real roots, $c_1e^{r_1t} + c_2e^{r_2t}$.
- $= 0$: double root, $(c_1 + c_2t)e^{rt}$.
- $< 0$: complex roots, $e^{\alpha t}(c_1\cos\beta t + c_2\sin\beta t)$.

Tip: these are the overdamped, critically damped and underdamped cases of an oscillator.
cards.searchQuery: discriminant cases second order constant coefficient ODE

cards.title: Solve $y'' - 4y = 0$, $y(0) = 1$, $y'(0) = 0$. (type $y(t)$)
cards.body:
$y = \cosh 2t$

Roots $\pm 2$ give $y = c_1e^{2t} + c_2e^{-2t}$. Then $c_1 + c_2 = 1$ and $2c_1 - 2c_2 = 0$, so $c_1 = c_2 = \tfrac12$.

Thus $y = \tfrac12(e^{2t} + e^{-2t}) = \cosh 2t$.
cards.searchQuery: solve y'' - 4y = 0 initial conditions cosh 2t

cards.title: Structure of the general solution of $y'' + py' + qy = g(t)$?
cards.body:
$y = y_h + y_p$

Here $y_h = c_1y_1 + c_2y_2$ solves the homogeneous equation and $y_p$ is any one particular solution.

Why: the difference of two solutions of the nonhomogeneous equation solves the homogeneous one.
Watch out: apply initial conditions to the **full** $y_h + y_p$, not to $y_h$ alone.
cards.searchQuery: general solution nonhomogeneous second order y_h + y_p

cards.title: Idea of the method of **undetermined coefficients**?
cards.body:
Guess $y_p$ with the same type of terms as $g(t)$ (and their derivatives), with unknown coefficients, then substitute and match.

- Polynomial of degree $n$: full polynomial of degree $n$.
- $e^{at}$: $Ae^{at}$.
- $\cos\beta t$ or $\sin\beta t$: $A\cos\beta t + B\sin\beta t$.

Watch out: include both sine and cosine, even if $g$ has only one.
cards.searchQuery: method of undetermined coefficients guess table

cards.title: **Modification rule** for undetermined coefficients?
cards.body:
If any term of the guess solves the homogeneous equation, multiply the guess by $t$ (by $t^2$ if it duplicates a double-root solution).

Example: for $y'' - y = e^{t}$, $e^t$ is a homogeneous solution, so guess $Ate^{t}$, not $Ae^{t}$.

Why: otherwise the left side produces $0$ and the coefficients cannot be matched.
cards.searchQuery: undetermined coefficients modification rule multiply by t resonance

cards.title: Particular solution of $y'' - 3y' + 2y = e^{3t}$? (type $y_p$)
cards.body:
$y_p = \tfrac12 e^{3t}$

Guess $Ae^{3t}$: $(9 - 9 + 2)Ae^{3t} = e^{3t}$, so $A = \tfrac12$.

The roots of the characteristic equation are $1$ and $2$, not $3$, so no modification is needed.
cards.searchQuery: undetermined coefficients y'' - 3y' + 2y = e^(3t)

cards.title: Particular solution of $y'' + 4y = 8$? (number)
cards.body:
2

Guess a constant $A$: $y'' = 0$, so $4A = 8$ and $A = 2$.
cards.searchQuery: undetermined coefficients constant forcing y'' + 4y = 8

cards.title: Particular solution of $y'' - y = t$? (type $y_p$)
cards.body:
$y_p = -t$

Guess $At + B$: $y'' = 0$, so $-(At + B) = t$, giving $A = -1$, $B = 0$.
cards.searchQuery: undetermined coefficients polynomial y'' - y = t

cards.title: Particular solution of $y'' - 3y' + 2y = e^{t}$? (type $y_p$)
cards.body:
$y_p = -te^{t}$

Since $r = 1$ is a root, guess $Ate^{t}$. Then $y' = A(t+1)e^t$ and $y'' = A(t+2)e^t$.

Substituting: $A\left[(t+2) - 3(t+1) + 2t\right]e^t = -Ae^t = e^t$, so $A = -1$.
cards.searchQuery: undetermined coefficients resonance y'' - 3y' + 2y = e^t

cards.title: Particular solution of $y'' + y = \cos 2t$? (type $y_p$)
cards.body:
$y_p = -\tfrac13\cos 2t$

Guess $A\cos 2t$ (the $\sin$ term comes out zero): $(-4 + 1)A\cos 2t = \cos 2t$, so $A = -\tfrac13$.

No modification: the homogeneous solutions use frequency $1$, not $2$.
cards.searchQuery: undetermined coefficients y'' + y = cos 2t

cards.title: Form of the guess for $y'' + y = \sin t$? (type the guess with constants $A, B$)
cards.body:
$y_p = t\,(A\cos t + B\sin t)$

$\cos t$ and $\sin t$ already solve $y'' + y = 0$, so the usual guess is multiplied by $t$.

Key idea: this is resonance, and the response grows linearly in $t$.
acceptedAnswers: t(A cos t + B sin t)
A t cos t + B t sin t
cards.searchQuery: undetermined coefficients guess y'' + y = sin t resonance

cards.title: How do you handle $g(t) = g_1(t) + g_2(t)$ with undetermined coefficients?
cards.body:
Find a particular solution for each piece, then add them: $y_p = y_{p1} + y_{p2}$.

Why: the operator $y'' + py' + qy$ is linear.

Example: for $y'' - y = t + e^{2t}$, guess $At + B + Ce^{2t}$ (separate pieces, separate checks for modification).
cards.searchQuery: undetermined coefficients sum of forcing terms superposition

cards.title: When does undetermined coefficients **not** work?
cards.body:
When coefficients are not constant, or $g(t)$ is not a sum of products of polynomials, exponentials, sines and cosines.

Example: $y'' + y = \tan t$ or $\dfrac{1}{t}$ forcing has no finite guess, so use variation of parameters.

Tip: UC is faster; VP is the fallback.
cards.searchQuery: undetermined coefficients limitations when not applicable

cards.title: Particular solution of $y'' + y' - 2y = 2t$? (type $y_p$)
cards.body:
$y_p = -t - \tfrac12$

Guess $At + B$: $y' = A$, $y'' = 0$, so $A - 2At - 2B = 2t$.

Then $-2A = 2$ gives $A = -1$, and $A - 2B = 0$ gives $B = -\tfrac12$.
cards.searchQuery: undetermined coefficients y'' + y' - 2y = 2t

cards.title: **Variation of parameters** formula for $y'' + py' + qy = g$ with independent solutions $y_1, y_2$?
cards.body:
$y_p = -y_1\displaystyle\int \frac{y_2\,g}{W}\,dt + y_2\displaystyle\int \frac{y_1\,g}{W}\,dt$, where $W = W(y_1,y_2)$.

The equation must be in standard form with leading coefficient 1.

Mnemonic: the first integral has $y_2$ with a minus sign; the second has $y_1$ with a plus.
cards.searchQuery: variation of parameters formula y_p Wronskian

cards.title: What must you check before applying the variation of parameters formula to $t\,y'' + y' = t^2$?
cards.body:
Divide by $t$ so the leading coefficient is 1: $y'' + \dfrac{1}{t}y' = t$.

Then $g = t$, not $t^2$.

Watch out: using the unnormalized right side $t^2$ for $g$ is the most common error with this formula.
cards.searchQuery: variation of parameters standard form leading coefficient one

cards.title: Derivation idea of variation of parameters: the two conditions on $u_1', u_2'$ for $y_p = u_1y_1 + u_2y_2$?
cards.body:
1. $u_1'y_1 + u_2'y_2 = 0$ (chosen to keep $y_p'$ simple).
2. $u_1'y_1' + u_2'y_2' = g$.

Solving this $2\times 2$ system by Cramer's rule gives $u_1' = -\dfrac{y_2 g}{W}$ and $u_2' = \dfrac{y_1 g}{W}$.
cards.searchQuery: variation of parameters derivation u1' u2' system

cards.title: Particular solution of $y'' + y = \tan t$ by variation of parameters (on $-\tfrac{\pi}{2} < t < \tfrac{\pi}{2}$)?
cards.body:
$y_p = -\cos t\,\ln\left|\sec t + \tan t\right|$

With $y_1 = \cos t$, $y_2 = \sin t$, $W = 1$: $u_1 = \int -\dfrac{\sin^2 t}{\cos t}\,dt = \sin t - \ln|\sec t + \tan t|$ and $u_2 = \int \sin t\,dt = -\cos t$.

Then $y_p = u_1\cos t + u_2\sin t$; the $\sin t\cos t$ terms cancel.
cards.searchQuery: variation of parameters y'' + y = tan t particular solution

cards.title: Wronskian of $\cos t$ and $\sin t$? (number)
cards.body:
1

$W = \cos t\cdot\cos t - (-\sin t)\cdot\sin t = \cos^2 t + \sin^2 t = 1$.
cards.searchQuery: Wronskian of cos t and sin t equals 1

cards.title: For the **Cauchy-Euler** equation $t^2y'' + \alpha t y' + \beta y = 0$, what trial solution and equation result?
cards.body:
Try $y = t^r$ (for $t > 0$): $r(r-1) + \alpha r + \beta = 0$.

Why: each term $t^k y^{(k)}$ gives $t^r$, so the powers of $t$ cancel.

Watch out: for a repeated root use $t^r\ln t$ as the second solution, not $t\cdot t^r$.
cards.searchQuery: Cauchy-Euler equation trial solution t^r indicial

cards.title: Exponents $r$ for $t^2y'' - 2y = 0$? (list)
cards.searchQuery: Cauchy-Euler t^2 y'' - 2y = 0 exponents

cards.title: ODE for a spring-mass-damper (mass $m$, damping $\gamma$, spring constant $k$, force $F(t)$)?
cards.body:
$m\,u'' + \gamma\,u' + k\,u = F(t)$

Here $u(t)$ is displacement from equilibrium. It comes from Newton's second law with spring force $-ku$ and damping force $-\gamma u'$.

Example: undamped and free means $\gamma = 0$ and $F = 0$.
cards.searchQuery: spring mass damper differential equation m u'' + gamma u' + k u

cards.title: Natural frequency $\omega_0$ of the undamped oscillator $mu'' + ku = 0$? (in terms of $m, k$)
cards.body:
$\omega_0 = \sqrt{\dfrac{k}{m}}$

The solutions are $u = c_1\cos\omega_0 t + c_2\sin\omega_0 t$, with period $T = \dfrac{2\pi}{\omega_0}$.

Watch out: stiffer spring means faster oscillation; heavier mass means slower.
cards.searchQuery: natural frequency spring mass sqrt(k/m)

cards.title: Angular frequency (rad/s) of solutions of $u'' + 9u = 0$? (number)
cards.body:
3

The roots of $r^2 + 9 = 0$ are $\pm 3i$, so $u = c_1\cos 3t + c_2\sin 3t$.

The period is $\dfrac{2\pi}{3}$ seconds.
cards.searchQuery: angular frequency u'' + 9u = 0 harmonic oscillator

cards.title: Amplitude-phase form of $u = c_1\cos\omega_0 t + c_2\sin\omega_0 t$?
cards.body:
$u = A\cos(\omega_0 t - \delta)$ with $A = \sqrt{c_1^2 + c_2^2}$.

The phase satisfies $c_1 = A\cos\delta$ and $c_2 = A\sin\delta$.

Watch out: pick the quadrant of $\delta$ from the signs of $c_1$ and $c_2$, not from $\arctan(c_2/c_1)$ alone.
cards.searchQuery: amplitude phase form harmonic oscillator A cos(wt - delta)

cards.title: Classify damping of $mu'' + \gamma u' + ku = 0$ by the sign of $\gamma^2 - 4mk$.
cards.body:
- $\gamma^2 > 4mk$: **overdamped** (two negative real roots, no oscillation).
- $\gamma^2 = 4mk$: **critically damped** (double root).
- $\gamma^2 < 4mk$: **underdamped** (complex roots, decaying oscillation).

Key idea: all cases decay to $0$ when $\gamma > 0$.
cards.searchQuery: overdamped underdamped critically damped oscillator discriminant

cards.title: Critical damping coefficient $\gamma_c$ for $mu'' + \gamma u' + ku = 0$? (in terms of $m, k$)
cards.body:
$\gamma_c = 2\sqrt{mk}$

Set the discriminant $\gamma^2 - 4mk = 0$.

Critical damping returns to equilibrium fastest without oscillating.
cards.searchQuery: critical damping coefficient 2 sqrt(mk)

cards.title: Classify $u'' + 6u' + 9u = 0$ (over-, under- or critically damped).
cards.body:
critically damped

The discriminant is $6^2 - 4(1)(9) = 0$, giving a double root $r = -3$.

Solution: $u = (c_1 + c_2t)e^{-3t}$.
cards.searchQuery: classify damping u'' + 6u' + 9u = 0 critically damped

cards.title: Classify $u'' + u' + u = 0$ (over-, under- or critically damped).
cards.body:
underdamped

The discriminant is $1 - 4 = -3 < 0$, so the roots are $-\tfrac12 \pm \tfrac{\sqrt3}{2}i$.

The solution oscillates inside the envelope $e^{-t/2}$.
cards.searchQuery: classify damping u'' + u' + u = 0 underdamped

cards.title: Quasi-frequency of the underdamped oscillator $mu'' + \gamma u' + ku = 0$?
cards.body:
$\mu = \dfrac{\sqrt{4mk - \gamma^2}}{2m}$

The roots are $-\dfrac{\gamma}{2m} \pm i\mu$, so $u = e^{-\gamma t/2m}(c_1\cos\mu t + c_2\sin\mu t)$.

Key idea: damping lowers the frequency below $\omega_0 = \sqrt{k/m}$.
cards.searchQuery: quasi-frequency underdamped oscillator formula

cards.title: What happens to $mu'' + ku = F_0\cos\omega t$ when $\omega = \omega_0 = \sqrt{k/m}$?
cards.body:
**Resonance:** a particular solution is $u_p = \dfrac{F_0}{2m\omega_0}\,t\sin\omega_0 t$, whose amplitude grows linearly without bound.

Why: the forcing matches a homogeneous solution, so the modification rule forces the factor $t$.
Watch out: real systems have some damping, which keeps the amplitude finite.
cards.searchQuery: resonance undamped forced oscillator t sin growing amplitude

cards.title: What are **beats** in $u'' + \omega_0^2 u = \cos\omega t$ with $\omega \approx \omega_0$?
cards.body:
A fast oscillation whose amplitude varies slowly: for $u(0)=u'(0)=0$,

$u = \dfrac{2}{\omega_0^2 - \omega^2}\,\sin\dfrac{(\omega_0 - \omega)t}{2}\,\sin\dfrac{(\omega_0 + \omega)t}{2}$.

The slow factor $\sin\frac{(\omega_0 - \omega)t}{2}$ is the envelope; its amplitude grows as $\omega \to \omega_0$.
cards.searchQuery: beats forced oscillator close frequencies envelope

cards.title: In a damped forced oscillator, what are the **transient** and **steady-state** parts?
cards.body:
The transient is $y_h$, which decays to $0$ because of damping. The steady-state is $y_p$, which persists at the forcing frequency $\omega$.

Example: for $u'' + u' + u = \cos 2t$, after a long time $u$ is just a sinusoid at frequency $2$.

Key idea: initial conditions affect only the transient.
cards.searchQuery: transient steady-state solution forced damped oscillator

cards.title: Definition of the **Laplace transform** $F(s) = \mathcal{L}\{f(t)\}$?
cards.body:
$F(s) = \displaystyle\int_0^\infty e^{-st} f(t)\,dt$

It turns a function of $t$ into a function of $s$, and derivatives into multiplication by $s$.

Key idea: constant-coefficient linear ODEs become algebraic equations in $s$.
cards.searchQuery: Laplace transform definition integral e^(-st)

cards.title: Sufficient conditions for $\mathcal{L}\{f\}(s)$ to exist for large $s$?
cards.body:
$f$ is piecewise continuous on $[0,\infty)$ and of **exponential order**: $|f(t)| \le Me^{ct}$ for large $t$.

Then $F(s)$ exists for $s > c$.

Example: $e^{t^2}$ grows faster than any $e^{ct}$, so it has no Laplace transform.
cards.searchQuery: Laplace transform existence exponential order piecewise continuous

cards.title: Linearity of the Laplace transform?
cards.body:
$\mathcal{L}\{af + bg\} = a\,\mathcal{L}\{f\} + b\,\mathcal{L}\{g\}$

The same holds for the inverse transform.

Example: $\mathcal{L}\{3 + 2e^{t}\} = \dfrac{3}{s} + \dfrac{2}{s-1}$.
cards.searchQuery: Laplace transform linearity property

cards.title: $\mathcal{L}\{1\} = ?$ (in $s$, for $s>0$)
cards.body:
$\dfrac{1}{s}$

$\displaystyle\int_0^\infty e^{-st}\,dt = \left[-\dfrac{e^{-st}}{s}\right]_0^\infty = \dfrac{1}{s}$.
cards.searchQuery: Laplace transform of 1 equals 1/s

cards.title: $\mathcal{L}\{e^{at}\} = ?$ (in $s$, for $s>a$)
cards.body:
$\dfrac{1}{s-a}$

$\displaystyle\int_0^\infty e^{-(s-a)t}\,dt = \dfrac{1}{s-a}$ when $s > a$.

Watch out: the sign is $s - a$, so $e^{-2t}$ gives $\dfrac{1}{s+2}$.
cards.searchQuery: Laplace transform of e^(at) 1/(s-a)

cards.title: $\mathcal{L}\{t^n\}$ for integer $n \ge 0$?
cards.body:
$\dfrac{n!}{s^{n+1}}$

It follows by repeated integration by parts, or from $\mathcal{L}\{t f\} = -F'(s)$.

Example: $\mathcal{L}\{t\} = \dfrac{1}{s^2}$ and $\mathcal{L}\{t^3\} = \dfrac{6}{s^4}$.
cards.searchQuery: Laplace transform of t^n n!/s^(n+1)

cards.title: $\mathcal{L}\{t^2\} = ?$ (in $s$)
cards.searchQuery: Laplace transform of t^2 equals 2/s^3

cards.title: $\mathcal{L}\{\sin bt\} = ?$ (in $s$)
cards.body:
$\dfrac{b}{s^2 + b^2}$

It comes from $\mathrm{Im}\,\mathcal{L}\{e^{ibt}\} = \mathrm{Im}\,\dfrac{1}{s - ib}$.

Mnemonic: sine has the constant $b$ on top; cosine has $s$ on top.
cards.searchQuery: Laplace transform of sin bt b/(s^2+b^2)

cards.title: $\mathcal{L}\{\cos bt\} = ?$ (in $s$)
cards.body:
$\dfrac{s}{s^2 + b^2}$

It is the real part of $\dfrac{1}{s - ib} = \dfrac{s + ib}{s^2 + b^2}$.

Example: $\mathcal{L}\{\cos 3t\} = \dfrac{s}{s^2 + 9}$.
cards.searchQuery: Laplace transform of cos bt s/(s^2+b^2)

cards.title: $\mathcal{L}\{\cosh bt\}$ and $\mathcal{L}\{\sinh bt\}$?
cards.body:
$\mathcal{L}\{\cosh bt\} = \dfrac{s}{s^2 - b^2}$ and $\mathcal{L}\{\sinh bt\} = \dfrac{b}{s^2 - b^2}$, for $s > |b|$.

Why: $\cosh bt = \tfrac12(e^{bt} + e^{-bt})$, then use linearity.
Watch out: the minus sign in the denominator replaces the plus in the trigonometric case.
cards.searchQuery: Laplace transform cosh sinh table

cards.title: $\mathcal{L}\{f'(t)\}$ in terms of $F(s)$?
cards.body:
$sF(s) - f(0)$

Integrate by parts: $\int_0^\infty e^{-st}f'\,dt = \left[e^{-st}f\right]_0^\infty + s\int_0^\infty e^{-st}f\,dt$.

Key idea: the initial value enters automatically, which is why Laplace handles IVPs directly.
cards.searchQuery: Laplace transform of derivative sF(s) - f(0)

cards.title: $\mathcal{L}\{f''(t)\}$ in terms of $F(s)$?
cards.body:
$s^2F(s) - s\,f(0) - f'(0)$

Apply the derivative rule twice.

Watch out: the second term is $s\,f(0)$, not $f(0)$ alone, and the signs are both minus.
cards.searchQuery: Laplace transform second derivative s^2 F(s) - s f(0) - f'(0)

cards.title: **First shifting theorem:** $\mathcal{L}\{e^{at}f(t)\} = ?$
cards.body:
$F(s - a)$

Multiplying by $e^{at}$ shifts the transform in $s$.

Example: since $\mathcal{L}\{\sin t\} = \dfrac{1}{s^2+1}$, $\mathcal{L}\{e^{2t}\sin t\} = \dfrac{1}{(s-2)^2 + 1}$.
cards.searchQuery: Laplace first shifting theorem e^(at) f(t) F(s-a)

cards.title: $\mathcal{L}\{e^{2t}\cos 3t\} = ?$ (in $s$)
cards.body:
$\dfrac{s-2}{(s-2)^2 + 9}$

Shift $s \to s - 2$ in $\dfrac{s}{s^2 + 9}$.
cards.searchQuery: Laplace transform e^(2t) cos 3t shifting theorem

cards.title: $\mathcal{L}\{t\,e^{3t}\} = ?$ (in $s$)
cards.body:
$\dfrac{1}{(s-3)^2}$

Shift $s \to s - 3$ in $\mathcal{L}\{t\} = \dfrac{1}{s^2}$.

In general $\mathcal{L}\{t^ne^{at}\} = \dfrac{n!}{(s-a)^{n+1}}$.
cards.searchQuery: Laplace transform t e^(3t) 1/(s-3)^2

cards.title: $\mathcal{L}\{u_c(t)\} = ?$ where $u_c(t)=1$ for $t \ge c$ and $0$ otherwise ($c>0$).
cards.body:
$\dfrac{e^{-cs}}{s}$

$\displaystyle\int_c^\infty e^{-st}\,dt = \dfrac{e^{-cs}}{s}$.

Key idea: step functions switch pieces on or off, so piecewise forcing becomes a sum of steps.
cards.searchQuery: Laplace transform unit step function e^(-cs)/s

cards.title: **Second shifting theorem:** $\mathcal{L}\{u_c(t)\,f(t-c)\} = ?$
cards.body:
$e^{-cs}F(s)$

The function is delayed by $c$ and the transform is multiplied by $e^{-cs}$.

Watch out: the shifted function must be $f(t-c)$. To transform $u_c(t)\,t^2$, first rewrite $t^2 = (t-c)^2 + 2c(t-c) + c^2$.
cards.searchQuery: Laplace second shifting theorem unit step e^(-cs) F(s)

cards.title: $\mathcal{L}\{\delta(t - c)\}$ for the Dirac delta, $c > 0$?
cards.body:
$e^{-cs}$

The delta picks out the value of $e^{-st}$ at $t = c$.

Example: a hammer blow at $t = c$ gives forcing $F_0\,\delta(t-c)$, which changes the velocity by $F_0/m$ at that instant.
cards.searchQuery: Laplace transform Dirac delta function e^(-cs)

cards.title: $\mathcal{L}\{t\,f(t)\}$ in terms of $F(s)$?
cards.body:
$-F'(s)$

Differentiating $F(s) = \int_0^\infty e^{-st}f\,dt$ in $s$ brings down a factor $-t$.

Example: $\mathcal{L}\{t\sin t\} = -\dfrac{d}{ds}\dfrac{1}{s^2+1} = \dfrac{2s}{(s^2+1)^2}$.
cards.searchQuery: Laplace transform t f(t) = -F'(s) example t sin t

cards.title: **Convolution theorem** for Laplace transforms?
cards.body:
$\mathcal{L}\{f * g\} = F(s)\,G(s)$, where $(f*g)(t) = \displaystyle\int_0^t f(\tau)\,g(t - \tau)\,d\tau$.

So $\mathcal{L}^{-1}\{FG\} = f * g$.

Watch out: $\mathcal{L}\{fg\} \ne F\,G$; the transform of an ordinary product is not the product of transforms.
cards.searchQuery: Laplace convolution theorem F(s)G(s)

cards.title: $\mathcal{L}^{-1}\left\{\dfrac{1}{s^2 + 4}\right\} = ?$ (in $t$)
cards.body:
$\tfrac12\sin 2t$

The sine transform is $\dfrac{b}{s^2 + b^2}$ with $b = 2$, so a factor $\tfrac12$ is needed in the numerator.

Watch out: forgetting the $\tfrac1b$ factor is a common slip.
cards.searchQuery: inverse Laplace transform 1/(s^2+4) sin 2t over 2

cards.title: $\mathcal{L}^{-1}\left\{\dfrac{1}{s(s+1)}\right\} = ?$ (in $t$)
cards.body:
$1 - e^{-t}$

Partial fractions: $\dfrac{1}{s(s+1)} = \dfrac{1}{s} - \dfrac{1}{s+1}$.

Then invert each term: $1 - e^{-t}$.
cards.searchQuery: inverse Laplace partial fractions 1/(s(s+1))

cards.title: $\mathcal{L}^{-1}\left\{\dfrac{1}{(s-1)^2 + 4}\right\} = ?$ (in $t$)
cards.body:
$\tfrac12 e^{t}\sin 2t$

The denominator is $s^2 + 4$ shifted by $a = 1$, and $\dfrac{1}{s^2+4}$ inverts to $\tfrac12\sin 2t$.

By the first shifting theorem multiply by $e^{t}$.
cards.searchQuery: inverse Laplace completing the square shifted sine

cards.title: Steps to solve a constant-coefficient IVP with the Laplace transform?
cards.body:
1. Transform the ODE, using the derivative rules with the initial values.
2. Solve the algebraic equation for $Y(s)$.
3. Use partial fractions or completing the square.
4. Invert term by term to get $y(t)$.

Tip: initial conditions are built in at step 1, so no constants are fitted at the end.
cards.searchQuery: solve initial value problem with Laplace transform steps

cards.title: Solve $y'' + 4y = 0$, $y(0) = 0$, $y'(0) = 2$ with Laplace. (type $y(t)$)
cards.body:
$y = \sin 2t$

Transform: $s^2Y - 0 - 2 + 4Y = 0$, so $Y = \dfrac{2}{s^2 + 4}$.

Invert: $y = \sin 2t$ (here $\mathcal{L}^{-1}\{2/(s^2+4)\} = \sin 2t$).
cards.searchQuery: Laplace transform solve y'' + 4y = 0 initial conditions

cards.title: Solve $y'' + 3y' + 2y = 0$, $y(0) = 0$, $y'(0) = 1$ with Laplace. (type $y(t)$)
cards.searchQuery: Laplace solve y'' + 3y' + 2y = 0 partial fractions

cards.title: Matrix form of a constant-coefficient linear system $x' = ax + by$, $y' = cx + dy$?
cards.body:
$\mathbf{x}' = A\mathbf{x}$, with $\mathbf{x} = \begin{pmatrix} x \\ y \end{pmatrix}$ and $A = \begin{pmatrix} a & b \\ c & d \end{pmatrix}$.

The origin is always an equilibrium. It is the only one when $\det A \ne 0$.
cards.searchQuery: linear system of differential equations matrix form x' = Ax

cards.title: If $A\mathbf{v} = \lambda\mathbf{v}$, what solution of $\mathbf{x}' = A\mathbf{x}$ results?
cards.body:
$\mathbf{x}(t) = e^{\lambda t}\,\mathbf{v}$

Why: $\mathbf{x}' = \lambda e^{\lambda t}\mathbf{v}$ and $A\mathbf{x} = e^{\lambda t}A\mathbf{v} = \lambda e^{\lambda t}\mathbf{v}$.

Key idea: with two independent eigenvectors, $\mathbf{x} = c_1e^{\lambda_1t}\mathbf{v}_1 + c_2e^{\lambda_2t}\mathbf{v}_2$.
cards.searchQuery: eigenvalue eigenvector solution linear system e^(lambda t) v

cards.title: Characteristic equation of a $2\times 2$ matrix $A$ in terms of trace and determinant?
cards.body:
$\lambda^2 - \operatorname{tr}(A)\,\lambda + \det(A) = 0$

The eigenvalues sum to $\operatorname{tr}A$ and multiply to $\det A$.

Tip: this gives a fast check of eigenvalues you have computed.
cards.searchQuery: characteristic polynomial 2x2 matrix trace determinant eigenvalues

cards.title: Eigenvalues of $A = \begin{pmatrix} 1 & 2 \\ 2 & 1 \end{pmatrix}$? (list)
cards.body:
$\lambda = 3,\; -1$

Trace $2$ and determinant $1 - 4 = -3$, so $\lambda^2 - 2\lambda - 3 = (\lambda - 3)(\lambda + 1)$.

Eigenvectors: $(1,1)^T$ for $3$ and $(1,-1)^T$ for $-1$.
cards.searchQuery: eigenvalues of matrix [[1,2],[2,1]]

cards.title: Classify the origin of $\mathbf{x}' = \begin{pmatrix} 1 & 2 \\ 2 & 1 \end{pmatrix}\mathbf{x}$ (node, saddle, spiral or center).
cards.body:
saddle

The eigenvalues $3$ and $-1$ have opposite signs, so one direction grows and the other decays.

A saddle is always **unstable**.
cards.searchQuery: classify equilibrium saddle point opposite sign eigenvalues

cards.title: Eigenvalues of $A = \begin{pmatrix} 0 & 1 \\ -2 & -3 \end{pmatrix}$? (list)
cards.body:
$\lambda = -1,\; -2$

Trace $-3$, determinant $2$: $\lambda^2 + 3\lambda + 2 = (\lambda + 1)(\lambda + 2)$.

Both are negative, so the origin is a **stable node** (this is $y'' + 3y' + 2y = 0$ as a system).
cards.searchQuery: eigenvalues matrix [[0,1],[-2,-3]] stable node

cards.title: Real eigenvalues $\lambda_1, \lambda_2$ of the same sign: what is the origin and when is it stable?
cards.body:
A **node**. It is stable (a sink) if both are negative and unstable (a source) if both are positive.

Trajectories run along eigenvector directions and bend toward the slower-decaying one.

Watch out: a zero eigenvalue is a degenerate case with a line of equilibria, not a node.
cards.searchQuery: node sink source real eigenvalues same sign phase portrait

cards.title: Complex eigenvalues $\alpha \pm i\beta$ ($\beta \ne 0$): classify the origin by $\alpha$.
cards.body:
- $\alpha < 0$: stable **spiral** (sink).
- $\alpha > 0$: unstable spiral (source).
- $\alpha = 0$: **center**, closed orbits that neither grow nor decay.

Example: $x' = y$, $y' = -x$ has eigenvalues $\pm i$, so orbits are circles.
cards.searchQuery: spiral center complex eigenvalues phase portrait classification

cards.title: Eigenvalues $-1 \pm 2i$: classify the origin (e.g. stable node, unstable spiral).
cards.body:
stable spiral

The real part is negative, so solutions decay like $e^{-t}$.

The imaginary part $2$ makes them rotate around the origin as they approach it.
cards.searchQuery: stable spiral complex eigenvalues negative real part

cards.title: Classify the origin of $\mathbf{x}' = A\mathbf{x}$ from $T = \operatorname{tr}A$ and $D = \det A$.
cards.body:
- $D < 0$: saddle.
- $D > 0$, $T^2 > 4D$: node (stable if $T < 0$).
- $D > 0$, $T^2 < 4D$: spiral (stable if $T < 0$).
- $D > 0$, $T = 0$: center.

Key idea: the origin is asymptotically stable exactly when $T < 0$ and $D > 0$.
cards.searchQuery: trace determinant plane classification phase portrait

cards.title: Repeated eigenvalue $\lambda$ of a $2\times2$ system: what shapes can the phase portrait take?
cards.body:
If $A$ has two independent eigenvectors, then $A = \lambda I$ and the portrait is a **star** (proper node): straight lines through the origin.

If it has only one, the origin is an **improper (degenerate) node** and $\mathbf{x} = e^{\lambda t}\left[(c_1 + c_2t)\mathbf{v} + c_2\mathbf{w}\right]$, with $(A - \lambda I)\mathbf{w} = \mathbf{v}$.
cards.searchQuery: repeated eigenvalue linear system degenerate node generalized eigenvector

cards.title: Stability criterion for the origin of $\mathbf{x}' = A\mathbf{x}$ in terms of eigenvalues?
cards.body:
**Asymptotically stable** exactly when every eigenvalue has negative real part.

If any eigenvalue has positive real part, the origin is unstable.

Watch out: purely imaginary eigenvalues give a center, which is stable but not asymptotically stable.
cards.searchQuery: asymptotic stability linear system negative real part eigenvalues

cards.title: How do you rewrite $y'' + py' + qy = 0$ as a first-order system?
cards.body:
Let $x_1 = y$ and $x_2 = y'$. Then $x_1' = x_2$ and $x_2' = -q\,x_1 - p\,x_2$.

In matrix form, $A = \begin{pmatrix} 0 & 1 \\ -q & -p \end{pmatrix}$, and its characteristic equation is $\lambda^2 + p\lambda + q = 0$.

Key idea: it is the same characteristic equation as before.
cards.searchQuery: convert second order ODE to first order system

cards.title: How do you get real solutions of $\mathbf{x}' = A\mathbf{x}$ from a complex eigenpair $\lambda = \alpha + i\beta$, $\mathbf{v}$?
cards.body:
Expand $e^{\lambda t}\mathbf{v}$ and take its real and imaginary parts as two independent real solutions.

Example: with $\mathbf{v} = \mathbf{a} + i\mathbf{b}$, the solutions are $e^{\alpha t}(\mathbf{a}\cos\beta t - \mathbf{b}\sin\beta t)$ and $e^{\alpha t}(\mathbf{a}\sin\beta t + \mathbf{b}\cos\beta t)$.

Tip: you do not need the conjugate eigenpair; it gives nothing new.
cards.searchQuery: complex eigenvalues real solutions linear system real imaginary parts

cards.title: How do you analyze an equilibrium of a nonlinear system $\mathbf{x}' = \mathbf{f}(\mathbf{x})$?
cards.body:
Linearize with the Jacobian $J$ at the equilibrium and classify the eigenvalues of $J$.

If no eigenvalue has zero real part (hyperbolic case), the nonlinear portrait looks like the linear one near the point.

Watch out: for a center in the linearization, the nonlinear system may spiral instead.
cards.searchQuery: linearization Jacobian equilibrium nonlinear system stability

cards.title: Steps of the **power series method** for $y'' + p(x)y' + q(x)y = 0$ near $x_0 = 0$?
cards.body:
1. Set $y = \sum_{n=0}^\infty a_nx^n$ and differentiate term by term.
2. Substitute and shift indices so every sum has $x^n$.
3. Set each coefficient of $x^n$ to $0$ to get a **recurrence** for $a_n$.
4. Express all $a_n$ in terms of $a_0$ and $a_1$.

Tip: collect all terms under a single $\sum$ before comparing coefficients.
cards.searchQuery: power series solution method differential equation recurrence relation

cards.title: Radius of convergence guarantee for series solutions at an ordinary point $x_0$?
cards.body:
If $p$ and $q$ are analytic at $x_0$, two independent power series solutions exist, converging at least up to the nearest singularity of $p$ or $q$ in the **complex plane**.

Watch out: complex singularities count. $\dfrac{1}{1+x^2}$ is smooth on the real line yet limits the radius to $1$ at $x_0=0$.
cards.searchQuery: ordinary point series solution radius of convergence nearest singularity

cards.title: Recurrence for series solutions of $y'' + y = 0$ about $x = 0$?
cards.body:
$a_{n+2} = -\dfrac{a_n}{(n+2)(n+1)}$

The $x^n$ coefficient of $y''$ is $(n+2)(n+1)a_{n+2}$, and that of $y$ is $a_n$.

The even terms sum to $a_0\cos x$ and the odd terms to $a_1\sin x$.
cards.searchQuery: power series y'' + y = 0 recurrence cos sin

cards.title: For $y' - y = 0$ with $y(0) = 1$, find the series coefficient $a_3$. (number)
cards.body:
$\dfrac{1}{6}$

The recurrence is $(n+1)a_{n+1} = a_n$, so $a_n = \dfrac{a_0}{n!}$ and $a_3 = \dfrac{1}{3!}$.

Thus $y = \sum \dfrac{x^n}{n!} = e^x$.
cards.searchQuery: power series y' = y recurrence a_n = a_0/n!

cards.title: Recurrence for the **Airy equation** $y'' - xy = 0$ about $x=0$ (for $n \ge 1$), and what is $a_2$?
cards.body:
$(n+2)(n+1)a_{n+2} = a_{n-1}$, and $a_2 = 0$.

The $x^0$ coefficient gives $2a_2 = 0$; the shifted sum $\sum a_nx^{n+1}$ starts at $x^1$.

Key idea: the coefficients step by 3, so $a_0$ generates one series and $a_1$ another.
cards.searchQuery: Airy equation power series recurrence a_(n+2)

cards.title: Guaranteed minimum radius of convergence of series solutions about $x=0$ for $(1 + x^2)y'' + y = 0$? (number)
cards.body:
1

In standard form $y'' + \dfrac{1}{1+x^2}y = 0$, and the coefficient is singular at $x = \pm i$.

The distance from $0$ to $\pm i$ is $1$.
cards.searchQuery: radius of convergence series solution (1+x^2)y'' + y = 0

cards.title: What is a **regular singular point** $x_0$, and what series do we try there?
cards.body:
A singular point where $(x - x_0)\,p(x)$ and $(x - x_0)^2\,q(x)$ are analytic.

Frobenius series: $y = x^r\sum_{n=0}^\infty a_nx^n$ with $a_0 \ne 0$, where $r$ may be non-integer or negative.

Example: $x = 0$ is regular singular for $x^2y'' + xy' + (x^2-\nu^2)y = 0$ (Bessel).
cards.searchQuery: regular singular point Frobenius method series x^r

cards.title: Indicial root of $x^2y'' + 3xy' + y = 0$ at $x = 0$? (number)
cards.body:
$r = -1$ (double)

Try $y = x^r$: $r(r-1) + 3r + 1 = r^2 + 2r + 1 = (r+1)^2 = 0$.

Watch out: with a double root the second solution involves $\ln x$: $y = x^{-1}(c_1 + c_2\ln x)$.
cards.searchQuery: indicial equation x^2 y'' + 3xy' + y = 0 double root
